topics.name: Regular Expressions
subtopics: Pattern Matching with search and match

questions.title: First Digit Finder
questions.description:
A validation drill scans a string for the first digit character anywhere in it using re.search and reports the exact character matched via .group().

Input Format:
One line: a string of 1 to 60 printable characters (may contain letters, digits, spaces, symbols).

Output Format:
If the string contains at least one digit: Found: <digit>
Otherwise: No digit

Constraints:
The line is non-empty and contains no tab characters.
questions.subtopic: Pattern Matching with search and match
questions.sourcecode:
import re

s = input()
m = re.search(r"\d", s)
if m:
    print(f"Found: {m.group()}")
else:
    print("No digit")

questions.title: Starts With A Word
questions.description:
An index builder checks whether a line begins with letters. re.match anchors at the very start, so a leading run of letters is captured; a leading digit, space or symbol fails the match.

Input Format:
One line: a string of 1 to 60 printable characters.

Output Format:
If the line starts with one or more letters: Starts with: <the leading letters>
Otherwise: No leading word

Constraints:
The line is non-empty.
questions.subtopic: Pattern Matching with search and match
questions.sourcecode:
import re

s = input()
m = re.match(r"[A-Za-z]+", s)
if m:
    print(f"Starts with: {m.group()}")
else:
    print("No leading word")

questions.title: All Numbers In A Line
questions.description:
A warehouse ticker pulls every integer run out of a line with re.findall(r"\d+", ...) and shows them space-joined on a single line.

Input Format:
One line of 1 to 100 characters containing at least one run of digits (digits may be embedded in words).

Output Format:
One line: every integer found, space-separated, in order of appearance.

Constraints:
The line is non-empty.
questions.sourcecode:
import re

s = input()
nums = re.findall(r"\d+", s)
print(" ".join(nums))

questions.title: Count Vowels With A Class
questions.description:
A phonetics lab counts vowels with one regex character class: every a, e, i, o or u in either case matches the class [aeiouAEIOU]. Count the matches.

Input Format:
One line: text of 1 to 100 characters.

Output Format:
One line: the number of vowel characters in the text.

Constraints:
The line is non-empty.
questions.sourcecode:
import re

s = input()
print(len(re.findall(r"[aeiouAEIOU]", s)))

questions.title: Hash Out The Digits
questions.description:
A redaction drill replaces every single digit character with a hash mark using re.sub.

Input Format:
One line: text of 1 to 80 characters.

Output Format:
One line: the text with every digit replaced by #.

Constraints:
The line is non-empty.
questions.sourcecode:
import re

s = input()
print(re.sub(r"\d", "#", s))

questions.title: Extract Every Word
questions.description:
A tokenizer splits messy text into word tokens: every maximal run of letters, digits or underscores (\w+) is one token, printed on its own line in order.

Input Format:
One line: text of 1 to 100 characters containing at least one word character.

Output Format:
One line per word token, in order of appearance.

Constraints:
The line is non-empty.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= len(line) <= 100, at least one word character
questions.sourcecode:
import re

s = input()
for w in re.findall(r"\w+", s):
    print(w)

questions.title: Log Level Spotter
questions.description:
A monitoring dashboard scans a log line and surfaces the severity tokens WARN and ERROR in the order they appear, using one alternation pattern with re.findall.

Input Format:
One line: a log line of 1 to 120 characters containing WARN or ERROR at least once.

Output Format:
One level token per line (ERROR or WARN), in order of appearance.

Constraints:
The line contains WARN or ERROR at least once; no level word is embedded inside a longer token in the tests.
questions.sampleinput1: INFO boot ok WARN disk high ERROR net down WARN cache
questions.input2: ERROR a ERROR b WARN c
questions.sourcecode:
import re

line = input()
for lvl in re.findall(r"ERROR|WARN", line):
    print(lvl)

questions.title: Mobile Number Verdict
questions.description:
A telecom signup form accepts Indian mobile numbers: exactly 10 digits starting with 6, 7, 8 or 9. Validate the whole string with the anchored pattern [6-9]\d{9} and print the boolean verdict.

Input Format:
One line: the candidate number, 1 to 12 digit characters.

Output Format:
One line: True or False

Constraints:
The line is non-empty and contains only digits.
questions.subtopic: Pattern Matching with search and match
questions.sourcecode:
import re

s = input()
print(bool(re.fullmatch(r"[6-9]\d{9}", s)))

questions.title: Contact Email Harvester
questions.description:
A CRM import tool harvests contact emails from a note with one pragmatic pattern: [A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,} written as a raw string.

Input Format:
One line: text of 1 to 120 characters containing at least one email address.

Output Format:
One harvested email per line, in order of appearance.

Constraints:
The line is non-empty.
questions.sourcecode:
import re

line = input()
for email in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}", line):
    print(email)

questions.title: Order Code Cleaner
questions.description:
A warehouse normalizes order codes by stripping every non-alphanumeric character (spaces, dashes, slashes, punctuation) with one re.sub call using the class [^A-Za-z0-9].

Input Format:
One line: a raw order code of 1 to 60 characters.

Output Format:
One line: the code with every character that is not a letter or digit removed.

Constraints:
The line is non-empty.
questions.sourcecode:
import re

s = input()
print(re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", s))

questions.title: Password Strength Classifier
questions.description:
A security dashboard grades passwords by counting four checks: (1) length at least 8, (2) contains a digit via \d, (3) contains an uppercase letter via [A-Z], (4) contains a special character - any non-alphanumeric character via [^A-Za-z0-9]. All four pass means Strong, two or three pass means Medium, otherwise Weak.

Input Format:
One line: the password, 1 to 40 characters with no spaces.

Output Format:
One line: Strong, Medium, or Weak

Constraints:
The password is non-empty.
questions.subtopic: Pattern Matching with search and match

questions.title: Due Date Extractor
questions.description:
A contract scanner pulls every DD-MM-YYYY date out of free text. Dates are zero-padded and appear literally in the text; re.findall with the pattern \d{2}-\d{2}-\d{4} collects them in order.

Input Format:
One line: text of 1 to 150 characters containing at least one zero-padded DD-MM-YYYY date.

Output Format:
One date per line, in order of appearance.

Constraints:
Dates in the text use exactly two digits for day and month and four digits for the year.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= len(line) <= 150, at least one DD-MM-YYYY date present
questions.sourcecode:
import re

text = input()
for d in re.findall(r"\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{4}", text):
    print(d)

questions.title: Masked Account Logger
questions.description:
A support tool masks numbers in transcripts: within every run of digits, all but the last four digits become X. One substitution does it - replace every digit that is followed by at least four more digits (lookahead \d(?=\d{4})).

Input Format:
One line: text of 1 to 100 characters.

Output Format:
One line: the text with each digit run masked down to its last four digits.

Constraints:
The line is non-empty.
questions.sourcecode:
import re

s = input()
print(re.sub(r"\d(?=\d{4})", "X", s))

questions.title: Duplicate Word Collapser
questions.description:
An editor macro collapses accidentally doubled words in one pass: a word, whitespace, and the very same word again (case-sensitive, whole words only) is replaced by a single copy through the backreference \1 in the pattern  (\w+)\s+\1 .

Input Format:
One line: text of 1 to 120 characters.

Output Format:
One line: the text with immediate duplicate word pairs collapsed.

Constraints:
The line is non-empty; no word is tripled or more in the tests.
questions.sampleinput1: this is is a test test line
questions.sourcecode:
import re

s = input()
print(re.sub(r"\b(\w+)\s+\1\b", r"\1", s))

questions.title: Config Pair Parser
questions.description:
A deployment tool parses settings from a line: every token of the form word=word is extracted in order with re.finditer over the grouped pattern (\w+)=(\w+) and printed as key: value using captured groups.

Input Format:
One line: text of 1 to 120 characters containing at least one word=word token.

Output Format:
One line per pair: <key>: <value> in order of appearance.

Constraints:
Keys and values are runs of letters, digits or underscores.
questions.sourcecode:
import re

line = input()
for m in re.finditer(r"(\w+)=(\w+)", line):
    print(f"{m.group(1)}: {m.group(2)}")

questions.title: Exact Word Counter
questions.description:
A search quality tool counts whole-word occurrences only: the pattern  cat  matches cat but not catalog or concat. Build the boundary pattern from the query word and count the matches from re.findall.

Input Format:
Line 1: the text, 1 to 120 characters
Line 2: the query word, letters only, 1 to 20 characters

Output Format:
One line: the number of whole-word, case-sensitive occurrences.

Constraints:
The text is non-empty; the query word contains only letters.
questions.sourcecode:
import re

text = input()
word = input()
pattern = r"\b" + word + r"\b"
print(len(re.findall(pattern, text)))

questions.title: Access Log IP Tally
questions.description:
A security analyst mines a mini access log. Each line starts with an IPv4-style address; extract the address with a regex (no splitting), tally hits per address in a dictionary, then print every address with its count, sorted lexicographically by the address string.

Input Format:
Line 1: an integer n, the number of log lines
Lines 2 to n+1: each line starts with an IPv4-style address like 10.0.0.5 followed by request details; no other dotted quad appears in any line

Output Format:
One line per distinct address, sorted lexicographically as strings: <address> <count>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 12; each address has four dot-separated groups of 1 to 3 digits.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 12, IPv4-style addresses with four groups of 1-3 digits

questions.title: Contact Field Normalizer
questions.description:
A data-entry pipeline cleans one messy contact line in stages, each with re.sub: first remove every double-quote character, then squash every run of two or more whitespace characters into a single space, finally trim leading and trailing spaces.

Input Format:
One line: the messy line, 1 to 120 characters, possibly with quotes and repeated spaces.

Output Format:
One line: the cleaned line.

Constraints:
The line is non-empty.
questions.sourcecode:
import re

def main():
    raw = input()
    step1 = re.sub(r'"', "", raw)
    step2 = re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", step1)
    print(step2.strip())

main()

questions.title: Expression Tokenizer
questions.description:
A calculator front-end tokenizes arithmetic expressions: numbers become integer tokens and each operator or parenthesis is its own token. One alternation pattern - digits first (\d+), then the operator class [+\-*/()] - pulls every token with re.findall in order.

Input Format:
One line: an expression of 1 to 80 characters containing only digits and the characters + - * / ( ).

Output Format:
One token per line, in order of appearance.

Constraints:
The expression is non-empty; multi-digit numbers must stay as one token.

questions.title: Triple Rule Validator
questions.description:
A signup gateway validates three record kinds by code. EMAIL values must be a full address like name@host.tld; PHONE values must be exactly 10 digits starting with 6-9; PLATE values must be two uppercase letters followed by four digits. Each value must match its rule ENTIRELY; print the boolean verdict per record.

Input Format:
Line 1: an integer n, the number of records
Lines 2 to n+1: a rule word (EMAIL, PHONE or PLATE), one space, then the value

Output Format:
n lines: True or False for each record, in order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10; values are 1 to 40 characters with no spaces.
questions.subtopic: Pattern Matching with search and match
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 10, values 1-40 characters, no spaces in values
